summary: Extends CalendarConnector with idempotent create (by atlas_event_id), update, and delete operations backed by a Postgres event index that maps Atlas event identity to Google Calendar event identity.

classification.why_platform: Provides a reusable Google Calendar integration surface with stable event lifecycle management. Carries no domain or workflow meaning — all business intent lives in the calling OpenClaw skill. The event index is a technical linkage table, not a domain model.
non_goals: Atlas as canonical source of truth for meeting content
Full internal event model in Postgres
Two-way sync from Google Calendar into Atlas
Advanced Google Calendar features: attendees, recurrence, reminders, conferencing
Manual Google Calendar edit conflict resolution
Update or delete by raw Google event ID as the primary API contract

consumes: CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID environment variable — operator-configured, never caller-supplied
Google Calendar API v3 events.insert, events.patch, events.delete
Existing calendar_connection and calendar_token rows from Sprint01/Sprint02 schema
Existing calendar_decision_log table from Sprint02 migration 002_write_capability.sql
platform_contracts.contracts.Dataset, DatasetMeta, ColumnSchema for read endpoints (unchanged)
provides: POST /api/calendar/events — idempotent create; returns CalendarEventOperationResult with status 'created' or 'existing'
PATCH /api/calendar/events/{atlas_event_id} — update supported fields; returns CalendarEventOperationResult with status 'updated'
calendar_event_index Postgres table — internal event index mapping atlas_event_id to google_event_id
Decision log entries for every create, update, and delete attempt via existing calendar_decision_log table
invariants: All writes target CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID exclusively — caller cannot override
atlas_event_id is the stable cross-system lookup key; google_event_id is never the primary input identifier
Every created Google event carries atlas_event_id in extendedProperties.private.atlas_event_id
PATCH to Google always re-sends extendedProperties.private.atlas_event_id to preserve metadata
Every create, update, and delete attempt produces a decision log entry
Deleted index rows are never hard-deleted — status is set to 'deleted', row is retained
Index status vocabulary is exactly: active | deleted | error
If Google event creation succeeds but index write fails, the operation returns an error (not silent success)
Token refresh follows the same lazy-refresh pattern established in Sprint01/Sprint02
Token values (access_token, refresh_token) are never included in any API response
failure_modes: NO_CALENDAR_CONNECTION — no connection or token row; 404
INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE — connection lacks write-capable calendar scope; 403
CALENDAR_TOKEN_EXPIRED — token expired with no refresh_token; 503
GOOGLE_API_ERROR — non-2xx from Google on create/patch/delete; 502
GOOGLE_EVENT_NOT_FOUND — PATCH resolved an active index entry but Google returned 404 for that event; index status set to 'error'; returns 404
EVENT_NOT_FOUND — PATCH called with atlas_event_id that has no active index entry; 404
NO_UPDATE_FIELDS — PATCH body contains no updatable fields; 400
INDEX_WRITE_FAILURE — Google event created but Postgres index write failed; returns 500 (orphaned Google event — known accepted trade-off; see risks)
ATLAS_EVENT_ID_CONFLICT — DB-level UNIQUE constraint violation on atlas_event_id insert; 409

provides: CalendarEventOperationResult — response shape for create and update success
CalendarDeleteResult — response shape for delete success
CalendarUpdateEventRequest — request body shape for PATCH
EventIndexRow — internal dict shape returned by event index query functions

consumes: token_store.upsert_token(conn, connection_id, access_token, refresh_token, token_expiry, token_type, scope)
token_store.write_decision_log(conn, operation, requested_at, target_calendar_id, outcome, google_event_id, error_summary, atlas_event_id=None)

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/calendar/events
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Create a Google Calendar event idempotently; returns 'created' or 'existing' in status field depending on whether the atlas_event_id already had an active index entry

exposed_surfaces.name: PATCH /api/calendar/events/{atlas_event_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Update supported fields of an existing Atlas-linked Google Calendar event; resolves the Google event via the internal event index

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/calendar/events/{atlas_event_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Idempotently delete an Atlas-linked Google Calendar event; marks index row as deleted rather than removing it

exposed_surfaces.name: token_store.get_event_index_by_atlas_id
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Lookup a calendar_event_index row by atlas_event_id for use by router handlers

exposed_surfaces.name: token_store.upsert_event_index
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Insert or reactivate a calendar_event_index row on successful create

exposed_surfaces.name: token_store.mark_event_index_deleted
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Set status='deleted' on a calendar_event_index row on successful delete or delete of already-missing Google event

exposed_surfaces.name: token_store.mark_event_index_error
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Set status='error' and record last_error on a calendar_event_index row when PATCH finds Google event missing

exposed_surfaces.name: calendar_api.update_event
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Call Google Calendar API v3 events.patch to update supported fields, re-sending extendedProperties to preserve atlas_event_id

exposed_surfaces.name: calendar_api.delete_event
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Call Google Calendar API v3 events.delete; distinguish 404 (idempotent success) from other errors

internal_flow.name: create_event_idempotent
internal_flow.description: POST /api/calendar/events handler. Validates connection and write scope. Refreshes token if expired. Queries calendar_event_index by atlas_event_id. If an active entry exists, returns the cached event reference with status='existing' without calling Google. If entry is absent or has status='error'/'deleted', proceeds to create. Calls calendar_api.create_event() which inserts atlas_event_id into extendedProperties.private on the Google event body. Writes index row via token_store.upsert_event_index(). If index write fails after successful Google create, returns INDEX_WRITE_FAILURE error. Writes decision log entry best-effort. Returns CalendarEventOperationResult with status='created'.
inputs: CalendarCreateEventRequest (atlas_event_id required, title, start_at, end_at required)

internal_flow.name: update_event
internal_flow.description: PATCH /api/calendar/events/{atlas_event_id} handler. Validates connection and write scope. Refreshes token if expired. Queries calendar_event_index for an active entry by atlas_event_id. If no active entry exists, returns EVENT_NOT_FOUND (404). Calls calendar_api.update_event() with the Google event ID from the index. If Google returns 404 (event missing remotely), calls token_store.mark_event_index_error(), records decision log with outcome='failure', returns GOOGLE_EVENT_NOT_FOUND (404). On success, writes decision log best-effort, returns CalendarEventOperationResult with status='updated'.
inputs: CalendarUpdateEventRequest (at least one of: title, start_at, end_at, description, location, all_day)
outputs: calendar_event_index status set to 'error' on Google 404

internal_flow.name: delete_event_idempotent
internal_flow.description: DELETE /api/calendar/events/{atlas_event_id} handler. Validates connection and write scope. Refreshes token if expired. Queries calendar_event_index for any entry (active or deleted) by atlas_event_id. If no index entry exists at all, returns CalendarDeleteResult with status='deleted' and google_event_id=None (idempotent success — never existed). If entry has status='deleted', returns CalendarDeleteResult with status='deleted' and google_event_id from index (idempotent success — already deleted). If entry is active, calls calendar_api.delete_event(). If Google returns 404 (already missing), calls token_store.mark_event_index_deleted(), records decision log with note about remote absence, returns success. On successful remote delete, calls token_store.mark_event_index_deleted(), writes decision log, returns CalendarDeleteResult.

internal_flow.name: token_refresh_helper
internal_flow.description: Shared internal function _get_valid_access_token(conn, connection, token) extracts the ~40-line token refresh block duplicated between get_events, create_event, and now update/delete handlers. Returns a valid access_token string. On unrecoverable token failure, updates connection status and returns an api_error response object. Callers check the return type: str means success, JSONResponse means early return.
outputs: valid access_token string | JSONResponse error (CALENDAR_TOKEN_EXPIRED or CALENDAR_ACCESS_REVOKED)

deferred_decisions: Whether to add a secondary index on calendar_event_index.status for filtering — not required at current scale; designer defers to implementer

Whether upsert_event_index on re-create after delete reactivates the existing row or inserts a new row — either is valid per specs; implementer may choose reactivation (simpler) or new row (cleaner history)

risks.impact: If Google event creation succeeds but the Postgres index write fails, a Google event exists with no index entry. CalendarConnector will treat a subsequent create as a new event (no index entry found) and create a duplicate. This is an accepted trade-off for this slice — no background reconciliation is in scope. The implementer must surface the failure as INDEX_WRITE_FAILURE and log the google_event_id for manual recovery.

Without extracting _get_valid_access_token as a shared helper, the ~40-line refresh block will appear in 4 handlers. Maintenance risk rather than correctness risk. Extraction is specified as a required implementation task.

risks.risk: atlas_event_id uniqueness relies on caller discipline
risks.impact: The DB UNIQUE constraint on atlas_event_id prevents duplicate index rows but does not prevent the caller from using semantically different events under the same ID. If OpenClaw reuses an atlas_event_id for a logically different event after the original was deleted, the re-create will reactivate or replace the old index row. The UNIQUE constraint surfaces conflicts as explicit DB errors rather than silent corruption.

If atlas_event_id has status='error' in the index, a PATCH request returns EVENT_NOT_FOUND (only active entries are resolvable for update). The caller must re-create before updating. This is consistent with the spec but may surprise callers who expect PATCH to work on an error-status event.

open_questions.question: Should the create endpoint return HTTP 200 when returning an existing mapping (status='existing'), or always 201? The specs document implies 201 for new creates only; returning 201 for an idempotent return would be misleading.
open_questions.resolution: POST returns 201 when status='created' (new Google event was inserted) and 200 when status='existing' (active mapping returned, no Google call made). Follows RFC 9110 semantics: 201 signals resource creation, 200 signals successful idempotent return of an existing resource.
